rationale:
dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=0.5, seed=1234, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=3000, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, rationale=iter-12 CEILING-CONFIRMATION PROBE (gradient-clip threshold / per-scan optimization regime) toward the iter-20 hard stop -- NOT hr-chasing. Change EXACTLY ONE knob: grad_clip 1.0 -> 0.5 (HALVE the gradient-norm clip on BOTH the amortized warm-start opt (solver clip_and_step) and the per-scan _fit_one_scene Adam opt). proj_kernel reverted 11 -> 5 (CONFIG default) so this is a clean single-knob A/B vs the iter-1 canonical config isolating the grad-clip axis. Everything else held at iter-1 canonical: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, img_n_bf=proj_n_bf=1, all sigmas at Wagner defaults, n_iter=400, lr=5e-3, train_n=200, val_n=6, seed=1234 (iter-6-confirmed stable). grad_clip stays >0 (mandatory: the 2304-view FBP adjoint overflows at grad_clip=0); 0.5 is TIGHTER than the mandatory 1.0 floor so it is overflow-SAFE by construction (a tighter clip can only shrink the per-step update, never let it explode).

STATE: CONVERGED to the 6-param structural ceiling. 11 iters all flat at SSIM ~0.9452-0.9470 @1, hr 0 (PSNR ~35.6 dB, ~1 dB BELOW the LD-FBP baseline 36.56 dB): iter-1 0.946237, iter-2 (img_n_bf 1->3) 0.945237, iter-3 (img_sr 0.02->0.005) 0.946177, iter-4 (proj_sr 0.02->0.0005) 0.945745, iter-5 (warm_start OFF) 0.945955, iter-6 (seed 42->1234) 0.946157, iter-7 (pretrain_epochs 3->8) 0.946953 [best], iter-8 (n_iter 400->800) 0.946240, iter-9 (lr 5e-3->1e-3) 0.945747, iter-10 (img_kernel 7->13) 0.946223, iter-11 (proj_kernel 5->11) 0.945929. This matches the documented dd-bf-supervised structural ceiling (capped 0.9502 with the SAME 6 BF params, every scalar flat).

TREND iter-10 -> iter-11: nothing moved SSIM. iter-10 widened the IMAGE-domain BF receptive field (img_kernel 7->13 -> 0.946223, hr 0), iter-11 widened the PROJECTION-domain BF receptive field (proj_kernel 5->11 -> 0.945929, hr 0). Both flat -> the ~0.947 ceiling is NOT a receptive-field limit in EITHER domain. Combined with the sigma/depth (iter-2/3/4), warm-start (presence iter-5, depth iter-7), RNG (iter-6), and per-scan-step/lr (iter-8/9) results, every CAPACITY-free and every OPTIMIZATION-budget lever is now bounded flat. The plateau is the 6-param BF CAPACITY vs the already-clean 2304-view FBP.

FAILURE MODE at SSIM 0.9470 (structural, not a tuning miss): the 6-param bilateral cannot beat an already-clean dense-view (2304-angle) FBP -- N2I is structurally FBP-bounded on 2304 views (hr~=0), because each per-scan fit only ever sees a 1152-angle (half-view) subset of the scan, so the half-view N2I information loss exceeds what 6 trainable bilateral params can denoise. No sigma/depth/warm_start/seed/warm-start-depth/per-scan-step/lr/image-kernel/projection-kernel setting clears hr=0. The remaining iters to iter-20 are CEILING DOCUMENTATION (probes that show WHY the ceiling holds), not optimization.

WHY THIS KNOB / NEW AXIS (untried): grad_clip has been pinned at the mandatory 1.0 in ALL 11 prior iters -- it is the ONE remaining untouched optimization-regime axis. It is distinct from lr (iter-9, which scales EVERY step uniformly) and from n_iter (iter-8, the step COUNT): the grad-clip threshold rescales ONLY the steps whose gradient norm exceeds the clip, so it changes the optimization TRAJECTORY (how aggressively large-gradient updates near the noisy 2304-view FBP adjoint are damped) rather than the global step size or budget. Halving it 1.0->0.5 damps the largest per-scan updates more, anchoring the per-scan BF fit nearer its init -- the same DIRECTION as the documented lr-down lever that lifts the high-capacity U-Net N2I (mayo-n2i 0.9508->0.9541 @lr3e-4), tested here on the 6-param BILATERAL which (unlike the U-Net) physically cannot overfit a single scan. If 0.5 still lands ~0.9462 hr 0, that bounds the ceiling along the grad-clip axis too and confirms the trajectory-damping lever (like the lr-down lever, iter-9) does NOT transfer to the 6-param BF.

HYPOTHESIS (named): GRAD-CLIP INVARIANCE. A tighter grad_clip=0.5 is expected to land at essentially the SAME ~0.9462 @1, hr 0 -- the 6-param BF fit is so low-DOF that damping its largest updates cannot change the converged per-scan optimum, which sits below the FBP regardless of trajectory. A flat result CONFIRMS the 0.947 ceiling is a 6-PARAM-CAPACITY limit, invariant to the per-scan grad-clip regime, ruling out 'clip too loose / trajectory too aggressive' as the cause. By construction this adds NO trainable capacity and stays overflow-safe (0.5 < the mandatory 1.0 floor), so it cannot escape the ceiling -- it can only document its invariance along the last untouched optimization axis. This is ceiling-documentation toward the iter-20 hard stop, not hr-chasing.

Per-image N2I (commit 1f4c3394): short amortized warm-start pre-pass (3 ep x 200 train) then per-scan Adam fit (400 steps) on each val scan's OWN half-angle measurements (GT-free), scored by evaluate_calibrated on the SAME L277 val scenes as every other Mayo method, at the DEFAULT inscribed-256px FOV mask (no fov= override). NOT amortized train-then-forward. Wall <=15 min target: grad_clip does not affect per-step runtime and proj_kernel reverts to 5; iter-1 ran 469s at this canonical config, expect ~470-490s, within the 1h sbatch wall and the <=15 min soft target.
